correctness.rationale: For m≥4 the initial degree partition isolates the clique attachment q0 (degree m), ordinary clique class Q (degree m−1), all degree-two path interiors and the leaf. The two path boundary fronts split from the one unresolved interval p_r..p_{n-r}, which becomes size≤1 at round ceil(n/2). For m=3 the ordinary triangle vertices have degree 2 and share a color with path interior; cases n=1,2 stabilize in rounds 1,2, and for n≥3 round three first separates Q from p1, after which the two-sided wave applies. The base cases and partition-stability convention were reconstructed. Independent WL implementation checked all 484 m=3..13,n=1..44 pairs (source also supplies independent partition checker).
residual_risks: Precise convention n = number of path vertices outside clique matters.
Induction, not finite regression, covers arbitrary n and m.

value.rationale: The exact stabilization time of a standard clique–path family is a motivated natural invariant for practical color refinement. The m=3 exception is not mere parameter substitution: a degree-2 collision delays separation and changes the entire small-n phase diagram. A complete formula over unbounded n clarifies the iteration mechanism and supplies sharp benchmark families.
residual_risks: If an unindexed thesis provides the identical formula, originality must be reconsidered.

final_claim: For m≥3,n≥1, L_{m,n}=K_m with an n-vertex pendant path has 1-WL depth ceil(n/2) for m≥4; for m=3 it is 1 at n=1, 2 at n=2, and max(3,ceil(n/2)) at n≥3.
limitations: Only ordinary uniform initial 1-WL; m≥3 clique, n outside path vertices; no higher-dimensional WL.
Bibliographic coverage of unpublished theses may be incomplete.
